title: Correct proration drift and quota-offsets in outbound billing exports
creator: Priya Nair
description: Symptoms: NetSuite invoice totals periodically diverge from Stripe/ledger by small amounts and sometimes show missing proration line items when customers are refunded or when quota/usage adjustments and rate-limit credits overlap subscription changes. Root cause appears to be a combination of timestamp skew between the meter-collector and billing export job, and an export transformation that collapses negative adjustment lines into aggregated totals before emitting NetSuite rows. This ticket implements a deterministic proration and export path and a short-term reconciliation job to repair exported records for the affected window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a new subscription (monthly) on a test tenant
2) Trigger usage that hits quota for a few hours and causes a rate-limited credit to be created
3) Mid-cycle, change billing tier (upgrade/downgrade) to force proration
4) Issue a manual refund against a subset of usage lines
5) Run the nightly billing-export job against that tenant and ingest into the staging NetSuite exporter
6) Compare Stripe invoice lines / ledger rows to the generated NetSuite export CSV for missing negative adjustment lines and timestamp-derived proration duration mismatches
root_cause_summary: Two interacting bugs: (a) meter timestamps produced by the new aggregator are at second granularity and are occasionally later than the subscription change event, causing proration to calculate an incorrect partial period; (b) the export transform merges small negative adjustment lines into a single 'net_adjustments' value which loses line-level identifiers required by NetSuite, preventing correct invoice-line mapping and reconciliation. Both lead to mismatched totals and occasional missing refund lines in NetSuite.
proposed_solution: 1) Change export pipeline to compute proration using canonical Stripe invoice interval start/end values when available; fallback to event timestamps only when canonical fields are absent. 2) Stop collapsing negative adjustment lines — emit one export row per original ledger line with preserved invoice_line_id and adjustment_reason. 3) Add a reconciliation job that replays ledger -> export transform for a configurable date range and emits a "corrections" CSV for NetSuite import. 4) Add unit and integration tests + end-to-end QA with synthetic tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Export rows include invoice_line_id for every ledger line (positive and negative)
Exports computed using Stripe's invoice interval fields where present; tests cover fallback behavior
Reconciliation job can produce corrections CSV and we use it to fix historical discrepancies for March 2026 window
Automated tests demonstrate zero mismatches for a representative synthetic workload (upgrade+refund+quota-credit)
implementation_notes: Modify services/billing-export/transformer to preserve original ledger_line_id and to prefer canonical invoice_interval start/end
Add e2e test in billing-integration that simulates upgrade+rate-limit-credit+refund and asserts NetSuite CSV contains three separate lines with expected amounts
Migration: script services/billing-export/migrations/regenerate_exports_2026_03.py to re-emit exports for invoice date range 2026-03-01..2026-03-07
Backwards compat: keep existing CSV column order but append invoice_line_id and adjustment_reason columns (NetSuite mapping will be updated in parallel)
